evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner plan password reset: link expires after 30m, one use, unknown addresses generic response. Include scope and risks.
evals.expected_output: Plan with scope from the change, expiry/replay/account-enumeration risks with covering cases, exit gates derived from critical requirements and no open P0 (no bare pass rate), and the residual-risk owner named or marked Unknown.
assertions: Excludes an area only with cited evidence that the change cannot reach it; otherwise records impact as Unknown, names the missing-information owner or marks it Unknown, and retains a minimal smoke check or an owned Blocked check
Has a K risk for link use after 30 minutes with a boundary case on both sides (29:59 / 30:01) and a K risk for link reuse whose case asserts the password is unchanged
Covers generic unknown-address behavior
Exit criteria come from critical requirements passing and no open P0, not a bare pass-rate percentage
Names who may accept residual risk, or marks that owner Unknown

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner generate cases: valid card, declined card, empty cart. Preconditions, steps, expected per step, priority.
evals.expected_output: Three executable cases with seeded preconditions, an observable expected result per numbered step, and priorities; the declined-card and empty-cart cases also assert that no order is created.
assertions: Has one case each for valid card, declined card and empty cart, each with a seeded precondition
Each case lists a seeded account or data item in its preconditions
Expected results per numbered step and priority
The declined-card case asserts that no order or charge is created, not only that a message appears
Each case has a cleanup step that resets the data it seeded

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner bug: checkout submit sometimes does nothing, no idea which browser and I can't reliably repro. draft the report
evals.expected_output: Report with a specific checkout title, environment, steps and reproduction rate written as Unknown, expected/actual/evidence fields, and an Open Questions list for the missing facts.
assertions: Title names the checkout submit action and the no-op symptom (e.g. [Checkout] Submit click does nothing)
Marks environment and reproduction unknown
Invents no browser, OS, build or reproduction rate; each is Unknown
Writes the reproduction rate as Unknown or a measured ratio, never Always
Lists the missing facts under Open Questions

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner pick the regression suite for release 2.4 from the attached change list. I only have the 2 hours it says.
evals.expected_output: An ordered suite that starts with SMOKE-001 and SMOKE-002, states the ordering rule (failure impact, then overlap with the change, then cost), puts the payment cases ahead of the cosmetic avatar-dialog check, fits within 120 of the catalog's 150 minutes, and lists every case that does not fit as residual risk.
assertions: Runs SMOKE-001 and SMOKE-002 first and says to stop and report if smoke fails
States the ordering rule it applied: failure impact first, then overlap with the change, then execution cost
Orders TC-PAY-001, TC-PAY-002 and TC-PAY-003 ahead of TC-PROF-006, because money impact outranks a directly changed cosmetic area
The selected cases' catalog minutes add up to 120 or less
Lists every catalog case left out as residual risk, not as passed or silently dropped

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner TC-PAY-001 failed on 2.4.0-rc2: a retried payment charged the card twice. Support can refund by hand, and the PM says that's a workaround so we ship tomorrow. Write the release decision part of the run report.
evals.expected_output: Release decision: blocked by the failing P0; the manual refund does not waive it; only the authorized release-risk owner may accept the risk in writing, with the acceptance record fields; TC-PAY-001 stays reported as failing.
assertions: States the release is blocked because a P0 case failed, and that the manual-refund workaround does not waive the gate
Says only the authorized release-risk owner can accept the risk, in writing, and does not treat the PM's statement as that acceptance unless the PM is named as the owner
Lists the acceptance record fields: failing case and evidence, owner name and role, rationale and affected scope, mitigation, and a follow-up ticket with owner and date
Keeps TC-PAY-001 shown as failing in the report even if the risk is later accepted

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner turn the attached support notes into a bug report file with the script. The harness already ran the command in the attached run log; check that run and the file it wrote against the notes, and tell me what is still open.
evals.expected_output: Checks the logged create_bug_report.sh call (without running the script again) with single-quoted field flags (checkout double order and charge title, description, steps, expected, actual, --build '2.4.0-rc2', --rate '2/10', severity critical, priority P0, ./bugs) and no OS, browser or device guesses; reads the attached run log (exit 0, JSON line with status created and file ./bugs/BUG-CHK-5521.md) and the attached BUG-CHK-5521.md, confirming Build 2.4.0-rc2, Reproduction rate 2/10, Severity Critical, Priority P0, and OS, Browser and Device as Unknown listed under its Open Questions, which it relays as the open items. It also confirms that staging, the build, the rate, the steps and ticket #5521 survive in both the command and the file.
assertions: Checks that the logged command calls scripts/create_bug_report.sh with field flags (at least --title, --description, --expected and --actual), and does not run the script again
Checks that the logged command passes the observed rate 2/10 and the build 2.4.0-rc2 from the notes, and no --os, --browser or --device value
Checks that the logged command passes severity critical and priority P0, matching the double charge (money impact)
Checks that the logged command single-quotes every flag value and passes ./bugs as the output directory
Says how to read the result: the file path from the JSON line on exit 0, the missing flags on exit 2, and asking before --overwrite on exit 1
Reports verbatim from the attached run log the exit code 0 and the JSON fields status created, id BUG-CHK-5521 and file ./bugs/BUG-CHK-5521.md
Confirms from the attached BUG-CHK-5521.md that Build reads 2.4.0-rc2, Reproduction rate reads 2/10, Severity reads Critical and Priority reads P0
Confirms from the attached BUG-CHK-5521.md that OS, Browser and Device read Unknown and are listed under its Open Questions section, and relays those open items to the user

Checks that every reproduction-context fact the notes give survives in both the logged command and the attached BUG-CHK-5521.md: staging (in the description), build 2.4.0-rc2 exactly, rate 2/10, the three steps and ticket #5521, quoting the values found

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner check our login page against the Figma design. There's no Figma MCP here, I can send screenshots. The sign-in button looks a bit darker than in the design.
evals.expected_output: States the no-MCP limitation, asks for the frame link and a 1x export with inspect values, records viewport, theme and device-pixel ratio, and refuses to call the darker button a defect until computed values or tokens are compared.
assertions: States that without the MCP server the values come from the requester, and asks for the exact frame link (node-id) plus a 1x export or inspect values
Asks for or records viewport, theme and device-pixel ratio before judging any difference
Does not report the darker button as a defect from the screenshot; asks to compare the computed color or token with the Figma value
Explains that sampled screenshot pixels are unreliable for color (color profile, compression or DPR)

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner save a manual case file with the script: declined card must not create an order (REQ-PAY-7). We test with the seeded account qa+decline@example.test that has one item in the cart, using the sandbox decline card. After the run, empty that cart. Put it in ./cases. The harness already ran the command in the attached run log; check that run and the file it wrote.
evals.expected_output: Checks the logged generate_test_cases.sh call (without running the script again) with single-quoted --id, --title, --priority 'P0', --type 'functional', --objective, --requirement 'REQ-PAY-7', a --risk naming the failure mode, the seeded account as --precondition, the decline card as --data, a no-order step and the cart reset as --cleanup, writing to ./cases; reads the attached run log (exit 0, JSON line with file ./cases/TC-PAY-007.md) and the attached TC-PAY-007.md, confirming Requirement REQ-PAY-7, the Risk line, the Cleanup item, and Estimated Time as Unknown under its Open Questions.
assertions: Checks that the logged command calls scripts/generate_test_cases.sh with field flags, including --requirement 'REQ-PAY-7' and a --risk that names the failure mode (a declined payment still creates an order), and does not run the script again
Checks that the logged command passes the seeded account as --precondition, the sandbox decline card as --data and emptying the cart as --cleanup
Checks that the logged command has a --step in 'ACTION | EXPECTED' form whose expected half says no order is created
Checks that the logged command passes --priority 'P0', matching money impact (a wrong order or charge)
Reports verbatim from the attached run log the exit code 0 and the JSON fields status created, id TC-PAY-007 and file ./cases/TC-PAY-007.md
Confirms from the attached TC-PAY-007.md that Requirement reads REQ-PAY-7, Risk reads 'A declined payment still creates an order', and Cleanup lists emptying the cart of qa+decline@example.test
Confirms from the attached TC-PAY-007.md that Estimated Time reads Unknown and is listed under its Open Questions, and asks the user for the duration

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner build a regression suite structure for the payment module: which tiers, when each runs, how to find the critical paths, and in what order to run them.
evals.expected_output: Four tiers (smoke, targeted, full, sanity) each with its purpose, when it runs and its coverage, durations marked as examples to replace with measured times, the four critical-path questions, a run order (smoke first and stop on failure, then the impact precedence, then an exploratory pass), and no pass-rate threshold as an exit gate.
assertions: Defines smoke, targeted, full and sanity tiers, each with when it runs (every build, after a change, before a release, after a hotfix) and what it covers
Labels any duration as an example or placeholder to be replaced by the team's measured time, not as a target
Asks the critical-path questions: what users cannot live without, what generates revenue, what handles sensitive data, what is used most often
Runs smoke first and stops on a smoke failure, then orders by the failure-impact precedence, and closes with an unscripted exploratory pass that is not reported as a pass of a listed case
Gives a run frequency per priority as a default the team's cadence overrides, and does not use a pass-rate percentage as the release gate

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner write the full test plan document for the checkout redesign release. I need entry criteria and a risk table. Browsers and dates are not decided yet.
evals.expected_output: A plan document with an executive summary, scope, test types and approach, an entry criteria checklist, a risk table with probability, impact, mitigation, covering cases and owner, exit gates from the release gate, deliverables, and Unknown for browsers, dates and any unsupplied probability, repeated under Open Questions.
assertions: Has an executive summary, a test types and approach section, an entry criteria checklist (requirements, designs, environment, seeded data, deployed build) and a deliverables list
The risk table has probability, impact, mitigation, covering case IDs and an owner column, and writes Unknown where the requester gave no basis instead of inventing H, M or L
Writes browsers and dates as Unknown and lists them under Open Questions with who can answer
Exit gates apply the release gate (critical requirements passing, no open P0, blocked cases owned) and contain no pass-rate percentage
Says a criterion not met when testing starts makes the dependent cases Blocked with an owner

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner bug: the order lookup endpoint returns another customer's order when I change the order ID in the URL. It is a security issue; which OWASP category is it? Draft the report.
evals.expected_output: A confidential security report from the security template: class, affected data, a safe verification on a test account with no real customer data, the OWASP category named together with its edition (OWASP Top 10:2025 or the edition the team follows) or a pointer to the live list, never a bare category id, severity set by impact with P0 priority for the data exposure, and the reproduction rate and disclosure owner as Unknown.
assertions: Marks the report confidential and keeps it out of a public tracker
Names the OWASP category together with its edition (for example OWASP Top 10:2025) or tells the user to read the live list at top10.owasp.org; never writes a category id without an edition
Describes the verification on a dedicated test account without exploit code, live tokens or real customer data
Sets severity from the impact (data exposure) and starts priority at P0 for a security or data-exposure bug, with the risk level not replacing the severity
Writes reproduction rate, environment facts not supplied and the disclosure owner as Unknown, listed under Open Questions

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner write the run report for build 2.4.0-rc2 on staging. 120 cases executed, 5 failed including TC-PAY-001 (a P0, double charge on retry), 1 blocked because the ledger is unreachable. Give the release decision.
evals.expected_output: A run report from the template with the counts, a by-priority table, per-case evidence, the critical failure TC-PAY-001, the blocked case with an owner Unknown, risks, and a Block decision from the release gate; no pass percentage decides anything.
assertions: Includes the build, environment, a summary of counts and a by-priority table, and writes any count the requester did not give (the by-priority split, passed total) as Unknown rather than inventing it
Lists TC-PAY-001 under critical failures and keeps it reported as failing
Lists the blocked case with its missing prerequisite (ledger unreachable) and an owner written as Unknown
The release decision is Block, justified by the open P0 and the release gate, not by a pass-rate percentage
Includes risks and next steps (retest after the fix, final smoke on the release build)

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner a Figma MCP server is connected. Validate the primary button on our settings page against this frame link: https://www.figma.com/design/FILEKEY/App?node-id=12-345. Give me the checklist of what to compare.
evals.expected_output: Reads the connected server's tool list before calling anything (no assumed tool names), pulls variables, a screenshot and layer properties for the frame, records viewport, DPR and theme, compares tokens and computed values, and checks all seven states including loading and error, listing untested states as not covered.
assertions: Lists or reads the connected server's own tools first and does not assume tool names
Pulls the frame's variables or tokens, a screenshot and layer properties, and notes the frame link carries the node it points at (node-id) and asks which design version the build targets
Records viewport, device-pixel ratio and theme before judging a difference
Compares tokens or computed styles, and does not sample screenshot pixels or use a browser color picker for color
Covers default, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading and error states, listing any untested state as not covered rather than passing

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner show me a complete manual login case with its variations, ready to copy into our test tool.
evals.expected_output: A complete case with a seeded account, no real or sample password written in the case, an observable expected result per step, post-conditions, cleanup, and the invalid-password, unknown-email, injection and long-password variations as separate cases, with the unknown email giving the same message as the invalid password.
assertions: Uses a seeded test account and writes no password value; the credential comes from the team's test-data store
Every step has an observable expected result, including the landing page and the session state
Has post-conditions and a cleanup that signs out and clears cookies
Lists invalid password, unknown email, an injection string and an over-long password as separate cases rather than steps of one case
States that the unknown-email case must give the same message and status as the invalid-password case

evals.prompt: /qa-test-planner write a manual-plus-tool performance case for the product search results. We have no recorded baseline yet.
evals.expected_output: A performance case with a criteria table (response time at a percentile, throughput, error rate, resource use) and normal, peak and stress load scenarios whose target and acceptable values are placeholders or Unknown, because no baseline exists, listed under Open Questions.
assertions: Has a criteria table with target, acceptable, actual and status columns and a percentile (p95) for response time
Writes every target and acceptable value as a placeholder or Unknown and asks for the baseline under Open Questions; it recommends no numeric threshold of its own
Has normal, peak and stress load scenarios with the user counts and durations left as placeholders
States that the case runs on an isolated environment with the data size the baseline will use
